content.text:
I tightened up `0.html` without changing how it looks on a normal desktop viewport: it is still a 400px black circle centred on the page. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

## What changed

- **No more horizontal scrollbar risk:** removed `width: 100vw` from `body`, which can overflow when a vertical scrollbar is present.
- **Better mobile height:** `height: 100vh` became `min-height: 100dvh` (with a `100vh` fallback), so the circle stays centred when mobile browser toolbars show or hide.
- **Circle scales down on small screens:** the SVG was a fixed 400×400px and got clipped on viewports narrower or shorter than that. It is now capped at 400px and shrinks to fit, staying square.
- **Accessibility:** the SVG now has `role="img"` and a `<title>`, so screen readers announce it instead of skipping it or reading nothing useful.
- **Minor CSS cleanup:** added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset and `display: block` on the SVG.

## Things to be aware of

- **The label is a guess:** I used "Black circle" as the accessible name since nothing in the file says what the circle represents. Change it if it has a meaning (a logo, a status indicator, etc.).
- **Hover tooltip:** browsers show an SVG `<title>` as a tooltip on hover. If you don't want that, swap it for `aria-label="Black circle"` on the `<svg>`.
- **Left alone:** the page title and the SVG `id` (`ae683f770`) are unchanged, as they look like identifiers something else may depend on.

I did not add dark mode support, since it would change the rendered colours.
